name: @downtrace/protocol
description: The ingestion protocol of Downtrace, which tells you when a change breaks the performance of your Node.js backend, before and after you deploy: JSON Schema, fixtures and generated TypeScript types

scripts.prepublishOnly:
node -e "const p=require('./package.json');if(!JSON.stringify([p.exports,p.bin,p.main,p.types]).includes('./src/'))process.exit(0);console.error('
  '+p.name+' publishes through publishConfig, which npm does not apply and pnpm does.
  Publishing from here would ship entry points the tarball does not carry, which is how
  @downtrace/mcp@0.1.0 went out broken (gh-421). Pack it first, as CI does:

    pnpm pack --pack-destination /tmp && npm publish /tmp/<tarball> --access public
');process.exit(1)"
